data.long_meaning: Pradyotana originates from the Sanskrit word 'Pradyot' which means 'to illuminate'. The prefix 'Pradyo-' represents the beginning or commencement of an illuminating truth or wisdom, making the name an inspiring reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge and spreading light in the world.

historical_references.reference: Pradyotana, a Shaka king, is mentioned in the Ashoka inscription of Girnar. He is believed to have ruled from around 130 BCE to 100 BCE.
historical_references.context: An inscription discovered at Girnar mentions a Shaka king named Pradyotana, providing evidence of the Shaka rule in Gujarat around this time.

historical_references.reference: Pradyotana, king of the Satavahana dynasty, is mentioned in the Allahabad Pillar Edict of Emperor Ashoka. His reign is dated to around 267 BCE.
historical_references.context: An inscription discovered at Allahabad mentions a king named Pradyotana of the Satavahana dynasty, indicating that he was a contemporary of Emperor Ashoka.
